generation_evidence.observation: Cockpit glass, seats and hull keep stable geometry through a long orbit; sparkle debris moves consistently.
Flat outlined characters sit on a rendered 3D set with checkerboard perspective that stays clean.
Mouth and eye sprites swap while the head outline stays identical.
The ship, LODESTAR lettering and orange stripe recur crisp across shots and look like one asset.
Vent tunnel and rings stay solid; sparkles are clean particles, not warped texture.
One continuous crane-up from inside the vault cutaway to the bank facade and street: rigid geometry, consistent perspective, signage 'COBBLE FALLS SAVINGS' and 'BANK' stays crisp in every frame.
CCTV monitor text (CAM 24, CELL BLOCK C - CELL 24, REC) is identical and crisp while the camera zooms and tilts; side monitor shows CAM 19 and a timestamp.
Cellmate head outline, hair and proportions are stable; only the mouth swaps between a small dark oval and an open teeth-and-tongue shape about every 4 frames.
Protagonist keeps identical shape and scale against the bunk during a push-in; expression snaps from smirk to closed-eye smile between f833 and f842; arms re-pose in steps.
Same vault door, gold lid, shelves and lamp reappear from several angles at 5, 5.9 and 20 s with identical geometry: one reusable 3D set, not re-generated images.
Lane signs and X-ray UI (LANE 2, STAFF EXIT, CURRENCY 97%) are legible and unwarped; the conveyor casts a hatched floor shadow but the 2D characters cast none.
Tree growth, leaves and bark stay coherent through the move; clean perspective and consistent geometry.
Zoom into the eye with a vector-clean outline stays sharp, then an iris-mask transition: a compositing effect.
Sheriff face is identical across frames, static mouth, the hat and glasses crisp; the interior details (turtle toy, beer cup) stay stable.
Sign text DAYS SINCE LAST CRASH is crisp and stable and numbers swap cleanly; no warping text.
Tyre rolls with physical bounce and shadow; cap man changes pose, with a hard outline unaffected.
Chop blast and ring explosion look like stylised particle or sim effects with a radial burst.
Whip pan from the board up a wall corner past banner and pavilion to the valley in about 0.7 s; perspective, banner and brick courses stay geometrically consistent with no blur or warping.
Blue banner emblem (white tiger, yellow chevron, fringe) and brick mortar lines are identical and crisp in two frames of one push-in; the same banner recurs at f66, f240 and f420.
Commander's mouth cycles through about four fixed drawn shapes in 1.1 s and his helmet lifts off the head on a bob: a layered 2D puppet, not frame-by-frame generation.
Characters stand on sunlit stone with no cast or contact shadow while the cart and railings shade the floor: flat 2D art pasted into a lit 3D set.
Mushroom cloud is a smooth painterly sprite with a flat white ring that darkens over 1 s, in front of a blocky low-res wall texture: stock-style VFX over an engine set.
Foreground grass changes shape and brightness between consecutive frames while the characters and arch stay put: real-time grass sway or LOD, not AI morphing.
Car interior and exterior are consistent solid 3D geometry across a fast camera swoop; car design, wheels and reflections stay stable.
Dashcam overlay text (REC, MPH, date, FRONT 1080P) stays crisp and the speed readout changes sensibly 54 to 0 MPH.
2D head with same outline is re-drawn per pose over a stable 3D scene; face shapes switch discretely.
Money, smoke and leaf bits move as particles; lamp, house, fence stay identical.
Same hero car interior and hero assets appear across scenes at different times of day.
Wall chart text (P-618, BAKER-MILLER PINK, recipe, EXACTLY!) stays crisp and identical through a push-in and a dissolve; no letter warping.
Calendar 1979 JUNE and COFFEE note stay legible; the cell inside the CRT screen matches the full-frame cell (window, bench, tally marks, drain) after the zoom-through.
Hall details (C-4 plate, hanging cable box, ceiling lamp, cyan brick wall, floor line) and the scientist's tie stripes stay identical while the camera pulls out; no swimming textures.
Debris cubes, cracks and the bar in the prisoner's hands keep consistent positions as the camera pulls out through the door; the guard enters with the same cap design.
Faces swap between a few discrete mouth and eye sprites (grin, laugh, closed arcs) with no in-betweens; the guard designs repeat exactly across shots.
Camera rises through the hall roof with consistent floor, skylight grid and roof gravel; clean perspective and no object morphing.
Steel arch bridge with lamps and rails stays rigid and consistent during a fly-in; rail geometry and perspective are clean.
Same hero model, cap stripes and colours reappear in every scene; limbs keep their length.
Newspaper text 'The Red Mesa Herald' is crisp, stable and readable across the take.
Calendar, thermometer and calipers stay readable; the coin gap grows smaller consistently; rails change colour smoothly.
Cliff walls show horizontal stripe or streak texture on the lower canyon, and the purple chasm water looks smeared.
The fireball looks like a volumetric VFX; the characters are then composited at the lower corners.
Pot, hull, porthole and oil stream keep consistent geometry through a long camera orbit; clean perspective.
Same hat badge, moustache and face outlines repeat identically between frames; only mouth/brow pose changes.
Galley props (lantern, porthole, pot, cabinet) keep rigid positions while camera drifts; crisp perspective.
STORM OIL label on tin stays crisp and spelled correctly; no warping text.
Explosion and smoke are flat polygonal comic shapes with black outlines, hat shapes float like 2D sprites.
Fast zoom out holds geometry steady; ship and tower stay stable while sea turns stormy, consistent with a camera move not a generated morph.
Piggy bank bursts into glossy shards, coins and dust that fly with consistent shading and lighting; pieces keep rigid shape from frame to frame.
Camera dives through a hand mirror: foreground heads scale up with parallax, background blurs with real depth of field, outlines grow with the object, geometry stays solid.
In-world sign letters N-I-N-E appear crisply one by one and stay readable; banknotes tumble and pile up without morphing; the MILK RUN 1000-1 plate stays identical.
Teller's face redraws as discrete mouth shapes (D, closed, round O) with identical outline, visor and banknote in all frames; no limb or texture drift.
Fast fly-through from the street into the telegraph nook keeps perspective, signs (BETS OPEN, horse-name board) and room geometry consistent frame to frame: a built set.
The same odds board with the 9 MILK RUN plate and the same characters recur identically across the video with matching text and colours: reused assets, not regenerated images.
Clean geometry of concentric streets and houses holds through a fly-through.
Characters keep identical outlines and shapes across shots; only eyes and mouth swap.
Counter digits and button details stay crisp and consistent.
Dozens of crowd members reuse the same few character assets.
Dissolve and ring glow added in compositing.
PHOTOGRAPHS sign and its tiny subtext keep identical spelling and shape across a 3.4 s push-in while defocused; no letter warping.
FIRST BANK sign, windows and cornice keep rigid perspective-correct geometry on a static camera; characters repeat the same costume details.
Flame wisps, glow ring and speed lines are flat 2D sprites over a 3D-lit blurred street; hat and holster shapes stay identical frame to frame.
Hat, gun, head and body move as separate objects with clean ballistic arcs and dust sprites; head size changes between poses by design, not by drift.
During a fast camera orbit frames come in identical pairs (1212=1213, 1214=1215): a held-frame cadence typical of keyed or on-twos output (estimate).
Eddie's mouth swaps between a closed moustache and an open-mouth sprite while outline weight, hat and straw stay constant; no morphing or drifting detail.
Clean geometry of shelves, counter and lamp holds identical across shots; same clerk model repeats
Ledger text legible and consistent between frames, but not checked closely
Character head tint shifts from warm to blue within a take while outline stays rigid
Wall drawings in ward are small repeating glyphs and shapes, stay stable
Pool water transitions into streak overlay, a deliberate stylised transition
Furniture, door, bookshelf and tile floor keep exact geometry through a camera move.
Small in-world text (CAREER DEVELOPMENT ROOM, LABOR LAW, SAFETY FIRST) stays crisp across shots.
Cat, cabinet, noticeboard and lamp move rigidly with parallax and do not morph.
Same boss, desk and room reused across many shots with identical details.
Faces swap between discrete expressions; mouth stays a fixed shape.

hook.first_frame: Smug boy in yellow vest with hands on hips beside a white toilet on a checkerboard floor, Earth in a porthole behind, toilet paper flying.
hook.first_3s: Hero smirks then closes eyes for ~1.1s, hard cut at 1.17s to exterior window, then a ship above Earth tilts and fires its thruster.
hook.first_frame_subject: protagonist posing with the key prop
hook.title_vs_first_line: Title restates the topic as a question; the first line gives the dramatic consequence of the same act.

story.structure: act first, explain at the end
story.real_fact_core: Spacecraft waste vented overboard freezes into glittering ice crystals and the vent gives tiny thrust, which could confuse star navigation.
story.protagonist: Rookie astronaut in yellow vest who breaks the flush rule
story.authority_or_antagonist: Mission Control and a shouting controller; crewmates in red and purple uniforms
story.explainer_turn: 'But how' at 32.9s, then 'Well, a spaceship toilet' at 35.4s

tone.humour: Absurd escalation from a toilet flush to being lost in space; exaggerated faces.
tone.deadpan_or_irony: Deadpan stakes with a rookie's smug eye-roll; faux-serious mission jargon.
tone.dialogue_style: Short shouted lines (It's a toilet! Who flushed?) inside fast narration; no pauses.

beats.name: hook
beats.said: Flushing a spaceship toilet means you never get back to Earth.
beats.shown: Hero beside toilet, then fast cut to ship above Earth and thruster flare.

beats.name: setup
beats.said: Mission Control schedules flushes; rookie ignores tonight's ban and scoffs at it.
beats.shown: Mission Control room, GO/NO GO screens, crew desks, rookie rolling eyes.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: At night he secretly flushes; morning, navigator sees hundreds of new stars.
beats.shown: Sleeping bags, hero at toilet, navigator in cockpit with floating sparkle stars.

beats.name: twist
beats.said: Stars are off the map, radio warns they are off course and drifting.
beats.shown: Star map card, radio, OFF COURSE screen, shouting controller, drifting ship.

beats.name: explainer
beats.said: Spaceship toilets just vent into space, and each flush pushes the ship.
beats.shown: Toilet room Q and A, waste vent tunnel, ship hull with thrust nub.

beats.name: payoff
beats.said: Spray freezes into ice crystals that glitter beside the ship.
beats.shown: Close-ups of boiling blob, freezing sphere, snowflake, glittering particle cloud by hull.

beats.name: ending
beats.said: Crew cannot tell fakes from real; without GPS they match real stars.
beats.shown: Crew in cockpit, phone searching, hero with telescope, scope LOCK, ship flies off.

hook.first_frame: Prisoner (orange jumpsuit, headlamp) stands in a bright cell, shovel raised at his side, gritted-teeth face to camera; small white-and-red X mark on floor; first caption word already on screen.
hook.first_3s: Shovel swings down; from 0.8 s floor cracks into glowing orange hole with flying rubble; face swaps shocked then smug; hop with scale pop at 2.2 s; slow push-in; dissolve at 2.53 s to tunnel cutaway.
hook.title_vs_first_line: Title compresses the premise (prisoner, tunnel, bank); first line gives prisoner and tunnel, the bank arrives in line two, so the title spoils part of the reveal.

story.structure: act first, explain at the end
story.real_fact_core: Corrupt guards use a prisoner as free labour: they let him dig, skip his bunk at headcounts and smuggle the loot out in lunchboxes, splitting it with him.
story.protagonist: Unnamed prisoner in orange jumpsuit with headlamp and brown hair tuft
story.authority_or_antagonist: Prison guards, secretly in on the scheme; cellmate is a sarcastic foil

tone.humour: Dry situational irony: a heist that cannot work, then guards running it; visual gags (donut guards, shades, plaid lunchbox) and the cellmate's sarcastic quip (estimate).
tone.deadpan_or_irony: Deadpan narration with a reversal; viewer is led to think the prisoner is foolish before learning the guards profit (dramatic irony); faces stay smug or blank.
tone.dialogue_style: Two quoted one-liners embedded in the narration (cellmate's sarcastic congratulation, guard's one-word verdict); no separate character voices evident (audio not reviewed).

beats.name: hook
beats.said: A prisoner's escape tunnel from his cell ends unexpectedly inside a bank vault opposite the jail.
beats.shown: Prisoner swings shovel in sunny cell, floor bursts into orange hole; tunnel cutaway; he rises in the gold vault; camera cranes out to bank facade and street.

beats.name: setup
beats.said: Asks why: he stays locked in, cannot spend loot in jail, and guards would find the bills.
beats.shown: Vault with hole, street cutaway, cafeteria with three inmates, corridor with protagonist in shades and guards behind him.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: He hauls cash back anyway; cellmate sarcastically congratulates him; he stashes it beneath the mattress and repeats nightly.
beats.shown: Vault cash grab, night cell with cellmate holding a noodle cup, protagonist on bunk with bills in his collar, glowing hole.

beats.name: twist
beats.said: Guards raid the block at morning, flip his mattress, find nothing and wave him through as clean.
beats.shown: Bright doors burst open, guards sweep the block, mattress flipped, nothing under it; close-up of sunglasses guard with plaid bag.

beats.name: explainer
beats.said: Reveal: guards supplied the shovel and left his bunk out of headcounts so he would do the digging.
beats.shown: Break-room guards with donut and CCTV monitor, glowing shovel on dark floor, guard with clipboard walks past, cutaway of prisoner digging.

beats.name: payoff
beats.said: Each morning the loot leaves through the front gate inside the guards' lunchboxes.
beats.shown: Staff screening lane: X-ray monitor shows lunchboxes full of cash; guard and woman in purple carry lunchboxes out the staff exit.

beats.name: ending
beats.said: Loot is split between guards and prisoner, who collects his half on release day.
beats.shown: Sunny street: group behind stacked lunchboxes; prisoner in brown suit walks in, arms up, big grin; last frame held, no CTA text.

hook.first_frame: Cartoon man in red cap and teal jacket stands on grass beside a road, holding a dark mitt-like object, a dirt mound in front of him.
hook.first_3s: He plants a seed, a huge tree bursts up and knocks him over; camera pulls out to a wide of the road with a car swerving toward the tree.

story.structure: act first, explain at the end
story.real_fact_core: Target fixation: drivers steer toward what they stare at, so a salient lone obstacle draws crashes.
story.protagonist: Tow truck guy and the sheriff (a comic escalation duo)
story.authority_or_antagonist: The sheriff, who repeats the mistake despite knowing.
story.explainer_turn: 'So how does this keep happening?' at 42.07s, then 'target fixation' at 43.7s

tone.humour: Absurd escalation: the fix makes it worse, tow driver profits, sheriff repeats the crash.
tone.deadpan_or_irony: Deadpan narration over slapstick; heavy irony in the arrow and the sheriff returning for a quiet road.
tone.dialogue_style: No quoted dialogue; fast narrated present-tense summary, very short sentences.

beats.name: hook
beats.said: Plant a tree beside an empty road and cars will steer right into it.
beats.shown: Man plants tree, it grows fast and knocks him over; car veers toward it.

beats.name: setup
beats.said: The road is dead straight for miles and this one tree stands alone beside it.
beats.shown: Man on grass by tyre; aerial view of straight road with lone tree.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: Somebody hits it weekly, so the town adds a flashing arrow, crashes double, tow driver profits.
beats.shown: Days-since-crash sign, giant neon arrow, wrecks, tow truck and lawn chair.

beats.name: twist
beats.said: The sheriff investigates, crawls at 15 mph and still crashes, then axes the tree.

hook.first_frame: Blurred protagonist at a desk with a small red FIRE button on a green mat, blue Japanese-style room behind.
hook.first_3s: Camera swoops to the big FIRE button, a mallet smacks it with spark lines, then pulls up and back to the worried seated protagonist, then boss with closed eyes.
hook.first_frame_subject: protagonist posing with the key prop
hook.title_vs_first_line: Title promises an unwanted job; first line makes the claim that firing is impossible, then teases something worse.

story.real_fact_core: Japanese law makes firing hard, so firms use pressure-by-idleness 'banishment rooms' to push staff out.
story.protagonist: unnamed 'you' office worker with black hair, blue shirt, dropped into a room with nothing to do
story.authority_or_antagonist: smiling grey-haired boss in dark suit and red tie

tone.humour: Mild; cheerful boss and drinks-with-umbrellas lounging contrast with creeping dread.
tone.deadpan_or_irony: Irony: paradise turns to isolation; smiling boss as villain; closing line is a flat moral.
tone.dialogue_style: Narrator in second person, fast and unbroken; no quoted speech.

beats.name: hook
beats.said: Firing is impossible in Japan, but companies found something worse.
beats.shown: Hand-slammed FIRE button on a desk, nervous employee, then smiling boss behind a button.

beats.name: setup
beats.said: Imagine boss leads you to tiny room: no computer, a clock, a guy on phone; job is nothing.
beats.shown: Office, door sign, empty desk, wall clock, man with feet up, boss holding red box.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: Sit until six; you're paid for this; at first it's paradise.
beats.shown: Protagonist grins at desk, phone shows pay, lounging top-down.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: Coworkers stare, emails stop, desk replaced, boss cheerfully checks in each Friday.
beats.shown: Open office, empty inbox, family photo, calendar, boss smiling in doorway.

beats.name: twist
beats.said: The corner guy seems happy, so you join him with feet up.
beats.shown: Man in corner, night tower window, two men relaxing with drinks.

beats.name: payoff
beats.said: One Monday he is gone, desk cleared, nobody says where.
beats.shown: Empty desk and chair, coworkers standing, door.

beats.name: explainer
beats.said: Law prevents firing but nothing prevents misery; they remove work and friends and wait.
beats.shown: Dark blue room, fire alarm with LABOR LAW tag, boss with mail cabinet.

beats.name: ending
beats.said: Nobody can do nothing forever.
beats.shown: Close-up of door sign; through window the lone worker sits at desk.
